newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls on Israelis, Palestinians to negotiate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls on Israelis, Palestinians to negotiate.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday criticised Israel for going ahead with a controversial housing project, voiced hopes there would be no violent Palestinian reaction and urged both sides to resume negotiations.

"I think that the Israelis understand the difficulties that we see with their going forward," Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said as Israeli bulldozers moved in to tear up a hillside for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Albright, briefing reporters before a U.S.-Russian summit in Helsinki this week, noted President Bill Clinton had said publicly that he wished Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had not decided to start the project.
Asked about fears of a possible violent Palestinian backlash, Albright said: "We are obviously concerned about the fact that violence is never an answer to the problems in the Middle East.

"We would very much want to see a return to the (negotiating) table," she said. "That is the only time that there has been progress in the Middle East ... when the parties are actually talking to each other at the table. And that is the way we would like to see things proceed."
Albright declined further comment and her cautiously worded remarks reflected the sensitive U.S. position as mediator between the Israelis and Palestinians.
